name: Ujazdowski Castle CCA
funding: State institution under the Ministry of Culture.
watch: 2020-24 directorship was politically contested, not a funding issue.
records_note: Publishes no annual reports or accounts that we found; the partners page shows logos with no dates and the board is not listed.

name: UKS (Unge Kunstneres Samfund / Young Artists' Society)
watch: Founded in 1921 by young artists. Runs experimental and political artist-run exhibitions and advocacy in Norway.

name: Ural Industrial Biennial of Contemporary Art
funding: State: Ural branch of the National Centre for Contemporary Arts, part of the Pushkin Museum since 2020; 6th edition (2021) budget c. 100m RUB; residencies sought Presidential Fund for Cultural Initiatives grants.
watch: 7th edition cancelled in Apr 2023 (announced by the city administration without explanation); team shifted to a research platform and art-industrial routes (2025 routes to Nov 2025). Founder-commissioner Alisa Prudnikova left to run GES-2 (V-A-C).
records_note: No records of its own were reachable, so this is its parent, the Pushkin Museum: yearly reports and accounts, logo-only sponsors, named trustees.

name: Usine Kugler (Fédération des Artistes de Kugler)
funding: Self-managed artist cooperative federation, City of Geneva Cultural Department, Canton of Geneva; non-profit foundation.
watch: Former tap and valve factory on the Arve River transformed by over 200 artists into an autonomous production and exhibition center.

name: Utah Museum of Contemporary Art
funding: Revenue $2.1M, expenses $1.8M (FY2024-25); Salt Lake County ZAP, Utah Arts & Museums, IMLS, Warhol Fdn, Eccles fdns, Zions Bank.
watch: Board president and $25k+ donor Rich Walje is ex-CEO of Rocky Mountain Power (coal-heavy utility).
records_note: Annual reports from 2018-19 to FY2024-25, audited statements to June 2025 and Form 990s are on its site, with named supporters and a listed board.

name: V2_ Lab for the Unstable Media
funding: Small foundation (2025–2028 plan) with structural funding from the Creative Industries Fund NL and the City of Rotterdam, plus EU project grants.
watch: Founded 1981. Dutch arts cuts after 2012 forced a reorganisation and ended DEAF, last held in 2014.
records_note: V2_ posts annual reports for 2007 to 2025, annual accounts for 2019 to 2023, its funders for 2025 to 2028 and its supervisory board.

name: Vanuatu Cultural Centre (Vanuatu Kaljoral Senta)
funding: A small statutory body funded by the Vanuatu government. After the Dec 2024 earthquake it relied on UNESCO's Heritage Emergency Fund (to May 2026) and online fundraising.
watch: Vanuatu's national museum, archive and fieldworker network. The Dec 2024 quake broke cases and destroyed Lapita pottery.
records_note: The centre's site posts no annual reports, accounts, named funders or board; its 2025 newsletter names funding types only.

name: Villa Arson
watch: Public national art school and contemporary art centre in a Brutalist building overlooking the Mediterranean.

name: Vitra Design Museum
funding: 2025-26: private foundation subsidised by Vitra AG; show sponsors include Maharam, Camper and IKEA Stiftung, plus the Design Circle friends.
watch: Independent foundation set up by Vitra and Rolf Fehlbaum in 1989; furniture-company money throughout.
records_note: The museum posts no annual reports, accounts, donor list or board; sponsors appear only as credits on individual exhibition pages.

name: Void
funding: Arts Council NI, Derry City and Strabane District Council, Future Screens NI, Garfield Weston Foundation, Halifax Foundation NI, Henry Moore Foundation, Ulster University; early build funded by Peace II.
records_note: The NI register holds annual reports 2023 to 2024 and accounts to 2025; the about page names funders undated and lists eight board members.

name: Wadsworth Atheneum Museum of Art
funding: $18.8M expenses (2023); FY2024: Travelers, Hartford Foundation, CT DECD, Henkel, Lincoln Financial, Bank of America, estates.
watch: Viking Fuel Oil Co. (heating-oil dealer, $500-1,499 tier) is on the FY2024 list. An ex-employee sued, saying she was fired for questioning a DEI initiative.
records_note: Annual reports 2009 to 2024 and Form 990s on its site, a FY24 philanthropy list naming donors, and a Board of Trustees page.
